name: json-api-reader
description:
Read one JSON API and keep only the fields you name. One request (GET, or POST with a JSON body), then one pass that walks to the list at ROWS_AT and keeps the FIELDS of each entry: `{rows, count, total, truncated, top, status}`. Nothing is built into a tree: a kept value is validated and copied to the output, and everything not named is stepped over without being parsed, so a field you did not ask for cannot appear in the output. An absent field is `null`; entries past MAX_ROWS are counted (`total`) and reported as `truncated`, not kept. TOP keeps fields beside the list, such as a paging cursor; this module makes one request and does not page. A response that is not 2xx fails the node with the host and the status, never the body.

COST (measured 2026-10-03 on this module as the platform compiles it): about 26 fuel per byte of response (7 for long text), plus about 1,000 per kept entry and 3,200 per kept field. 100 entries of 350 bytes keeping 3 fields: 1.9 M; 1,000 such entries keeping 100: 9.0 M, keeping all 1,000: 18.4 M; a 4 MB response keeping 100 entries: 27.7 M. The installed limit covers about 100 entries of 1 KB; for a larger response set `max_fuel` in the node's config. Text that is stepped over is not checked to be valid JSON; every kept value, and the structure on the way to it, is.

CREDENTIALS: the module never holds one. A HEADERS value or a string inside BODY may be a vault:// reference; the host replaces it when the request is sent.

GRANTS: this template installs with NO allowed hosts and no secrets, so it can reach nothing until you say what it may reach: after installing, set the API's host with update_module_hosts and the secret paths with update_module_secrets (list_connections shows the reference and the paths for a connected service). Use one installed copy per API, so a credential can only ever be sent to the host it belongs to.

block.reads_by_post: some APIs take a read query as a POST body (GraphQL, search endpoints)

URL.description: The https:// URL to request, query string included.

METHOD.description: GET, or POST for an API that takes its query in a JSON body. Nothing else: this module reads.

HEADERS.description: Request headers, name to value. A value may be a vault:// reference (for example {"Authorization": "vault://oauth/..."}); the host replaces it when the request is sent. At most 16.

BODY.description: POST only: the JSON body. A string value anywhere inside it may be a vault:// reference. Sent as application/json.

ROWS_AT.description: Dotted path to the list in the response ("data.items"). Omit when the response itself is the list. A path that leads to one object yields one row.

FIELDS.description: The fields of each entry to keep: a list of dotted paths (["id", "owner.name"], each kept under its last segment) or an object of output name to path ({"owner": "owner.name"}). 1 to 32.

TOP.description: Fields beside the list to keep, in the same two forms as FIELDS, with paths from the top of the response ({"next": "data.next_cursor"}). Needs ROWS_AT.

MAX_ROWS.description: Entries kept. The rest are counted in `total` and `truncated` is true.
